candidates.title: Directed codeword separation with assignment-preserving geometry
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the checked codebook gradient is zero or nonfinite, if swapping source and target leaves the loss unchanged under the checker, or if the frozen evaluation shows any increase in level-0 Gini, a decrease in L1-to-L2 branches per code, increased train-to-test frequency drift, decreased sequence information, or no rise in pair-level ER.
candidates.risk: The selected codewords may already exceed the margin for most transitions, making the term ineffective; otherwise repulsion may distort Voronoi cells, alter level-0 occupancy or prefix branching, and reduce sequence information even while preserving pair separation.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The penalty pushes selected codewords apart when their distance is below the margin. Its gradient is repulsive, never attractive, so it cannot directly pull a transition's two selected codewords together. Nearest-codeword indices are discrete and stop-gradient; epsilon stabilizes the distance derivative.

candidates.title: Directed conditional assignment entropy with balanced source usage
candidates.falsifier: The checker should confirm zero source, target, and codebook gradients; any proposal that claims this term changes trained SIDs is falsified if assignments and exported codes remain identical to control.
candidates.risk: This mechanism fails the required gradient-target contract: assignment statistics are nondifferentiable with the supplied interface, so it cannot affect training or exported SIDs. Its presence can only diagnose whether the desired assignment statistics are compatible with the current assignments.
candidates.codebook_interaction: This objective is computed only from detached integer assignments and has no differentiable path to the codebook. It therefore cannot pull transition codewords together, but it also cannot train or change the codebook. It is a probe-only candidate, not eligible for a cold run under the measured host behavior.

candidates.title: Behaviour-conditioned residual transport projected away from pair convergence
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the checker finds a zero or nonfinite codebook gradient, if swapping source and target does not change the loss, or if the frozen evaluation violates any measured requirement (level-0 Gini no higher than control, at least control's L1-to-L2 branches per code, no greater train-to-test frequency drift, no lower sequence information) or fails to raise pair-level ER.
candidates.risk: The tangential signal may be weak or noisy when residuals are small, and codewords selected by many transitions may drift together indirectly. It may also improve pair separation while damaging level-0 usage, prefix branching, frequency stability, or sequence information; no downstream benefit is assumed.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The loss applies a residual-conditioned tangential update to the source-selected codeword relative to the codebook centroid; the projection removes the residual-parallel component. The selected index is stop-gradient, and the update is anchored to the source-selected codeword rather than an attractive shared pair prototype, so it does not directly pull the transition's two endpoint codewords together. Indirect convergence through shared codeword updates remains possible and must be checked.
